lines.text: In this lesson, you will learn to complete bubble sort with nested loops, sort in either order, and measure how the number of comparisons grows with the list size.
One pass puts the largest at the end.
Repeat the pass (n − 1) times and every value reaches its place: that’s bubble sort.
Change > to < and the list sorts biggest-first — perfect for a leaderboard.
Bubble sort makes about n × n comparisons.
Double the list and the work roughly quadruples.
For 1,000 items that’s about a million comparisons.
Real apps use cleverer sorts (like merge sort) that take about n × log n steps.
Bubble sort is great for learning because it’s easy to see.
Nested loops in Python: the outer loop repeats the pass, the inner loop compares neighbours.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
